DJI Neo 3 Leak Lists a Square Sensor and a 42 g Weight Gain

By Amy Porter
October 4, 2026
Facebook
X
Pinterest
WhatsApp

    Quick Facts:

    • Story: DJI Neo 3 leak, a printed marketing sheet posted to X on October 1, 2026.
    • Status: Unannounced. DJI has not confirmed the drone, a price, or a launch date.
    • Sensor (leaked): 1/1.1-inch square, the same size and shape as the Osmo Action 6.
    • Weight (listed): 192.7 g, against 151 g for the Neo 2.
    • Zoom (leaked): 2x lossless, plus native vertical shooting.
    • Controller (leaked): DJI RC Mini, a name with an existing FCC grant.
    • US status: No FCC grant found for the Neo 3, so an official US sale looks unlikely.
    • Missing: Price, launch date, video resolution, and flight time.

     5 min read

    In This Article

    1. Overview
    2. What the DJI Neo 3 Leak Says
    3. Why a Square Sensor Matters for Vertical Video
    4. DJI Neo 3 vs. Neo 2
    5. What This DJI Neo 3 Leak Means for You
    6. Final Thoughts
    7. FAQ

    Overview

    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 7:51
    Instaread

    The newest DJI Neo 3 leak is a photo of a printed marketing sheet. Leaker Igor Bogdanov posted it on X on October 1, 2026. The sheet lists a square 1/1.1-inch sensor, 2x lossless zoom, and native vertical shooting for DJI’s next mini drone. Because DJI has not announced the drone, every figure here is unconfirmed.

    Bogdanov also surfaced a supposed Chinese registration listing dated September 21. According to Notebookcheck, it puts the Neo 3 at 192.7 g. The DJI Neo 2 weighs 151 g, so the new drone gains about 42 g. Treat the numbers as a lead, not a spec sheet, because both leaks trace to one source.

    For photographers, the sensor is the interesting part. The Osmo Action 6 already uses a 1/1.1-inch square sensor. Also, DJI lists it in the Osmo Action 6 specs. A square chip records portrait and landscape video without turning the camera. However, you will probably not buy this drone in the US. DroneXL finds no FCC grant for the Neo 3.

    Neo-style drones and the square-sensor camera you can buy now

    If you want a Neo-style drone today, Amazon lists the Neo 2 and the DJI Neo Fly More Combo, the original Neo. The DJI Osmo Action 6 Standard Combo carries this sensor size through Amazon sellers.

    What the DJI Neo 3 Leak Says

    Each claim appears below with its source and its status.

    Claim Source Status
    Square 1/1.1-inch sensor, 2x lossless zoom, native vertical shooting Marketing sheet posted by Igor Bogdanov, October 1 Single-source leak
    192.7 g weight Registration listing dated September 21, reported by Notebookcheck Single-source leak
    DJI RC Mini controller Retail box photo posted September 15; FCC grant dated December 19, 2025 Controller grant exists; Neo 3 pairing unconfirmed
    Omnidirectional obstacle sensing, SelfieShot 2.0, faster ActiveTrack Marketing sheet Single-source leak
    Price and launch date None Not announced

    Leaks in this line have missed before. On September 21, DroneXL called a separate Neo 3 image recycled box art with AI-drawn battery vents. Notably, Bogdanov did not post it. A source’s track record matters more than the number of outlets repeating a claim.

    The sheet also leaves gaps. It lists no video resolution, bitrate, aperture, or flight time.

    Why a Square Sensor Matters for Vertical Video

    A square sensor works like a 1:1 canvas. The camera crops a 9:16 or 16:9 frame from it, so the lens never needs to rotate. DJI’s Osmo Action 6 shows the method. DJI lists 4K Custom video at 3840 x 3840 and vertical 4K at 2160 x 3840 at up to 120 fps.

    The 2x lossless zoom line needs care. DJI describes the Osmo Action 6 zoom as digital, with a maximum of 2x in video. I read the Neo 3 line the same way: a crop from a large sensor, not an optical lens. The sheet does not confirm this, though.

    A bigger sensor helps in dim light, but only if the lens and processing keep pace. Without a leaked aperture or bitrate, sensor size tells you less than it seems to. For a square chip in a shipping camera, read our Osmo Action 6 coverage.

    DJI Neo 3 vs. Neo 2

    DJI published its numbers for the Neo 2, so it is the baseline. Leaked values fill the Neo 3 column, while gaps are marked plainly.

    Item DJI Neo 2 Neo 3 (leaked)
    Sensor 1/2-inch CMOS 1/1.1-inch square
    Weight 151 g (160 g with transceiver) 192.7 g
    Video 4K at 60 fps Not listed
    Controller RC-N3 RC Mini
    Release November 13, 2025 (Europe, Canada, Brazil) Not announced

    At 41.7 g, the gain is about 28% more mass, per Notebookcheck’s math. However, 192.7 g still sits under 250 g, the weight at which FAA registration starts for recreational flyers. Therefore, the added weight does not change your recreational registration status.

    The controller matters more. A Neo 2 combo ships with the RC-N3, which needs a phone clipped in for live video. In contrast, the leaked box shows a remote with its own small screen.

    What This DJI Neo 3 Leak Means for You

    First, the US question. DroneXL lists no Neo 3 among DJI’s pre-cutoff FCC grants. So DJI looks unable to sell it here through normal channels. Since the FCC Covered List froze new DJI authorizations in December 2025, the pattern repeats. Our DJI drone ban for US buyers explainer covers the rules. Next, the DJI product blocked from US sale report shows the same leak-to-lockout path.

    Second, the Neo 2 shows grants fall short. DroneXL says DJI skipped an official US launch for it, even though the drone received FCC certification. Retailers still list the DJI Neo 2 on Amazon. Our best drones for photography in 2026 guide profiles the original Neo as its beginner pick.

    Third, vertical video does not need a drone. If you want this sensor now, the Osmo Action 6 offers the same size and shape. Our reporting says DJI will not sell it officially in the US, but third-party retailers stock it. Before you buy, check the seller, the return policy, and the warranty.

    If you fly the original Neo, the DJI Neo Two-Way Charging Hub lists Neo compatibility. An action camera needs fast storage. Because the Osmo Action 6 takes microSD cards up to 1 TB, a SanDisk Extreme 256GB card fits. A ULANZI mini tripod with a rotating phone clip holds a phone for vertical or horizontal framing.

    Final Thoughts

    The DJI Neo 3 leak describes a sensible step for a beginner drone. A bigger sensor, a screen on the remote, and vertical video built in match how phone-first creators shoot today. I would still wait for DJI to confirm anything before you change a buying plan.

    My worry is the source. One leaker supplied the sheet and the weight, and neither has a second confirmation. Therefore, this DJI Neo 3 leak needs a DJI announcement. The missing price, date, and video specs leave real questions open.

    For US readers, the advice is short. Instead of waiting, buy a current Neo-style drone if you need one now. Meanwhile, treat the Neo 3 as news from overseas. If DJI announces it, we will update this page. The sensor is the detail worth watching, because it would move vertical video quality forward for small cameras.

    FAQ

    When is the DJI Neo 3 release date?

    DJI has not announced one. A registration listing shows a production date of September 21, 2026, which is not a launch date. Treat any specific date as a guess.

    What sensor does the DJI Neo 3 have?

    The leaked marketing sheet lists a 1/1.1-inch square chip. A sensor of the same size and shape sits in the Osmo Action 6. DJI has not confirmed the Neo 3 sensor.

    How much does the DJI Neo 3 weigh compared with the Neo 2?

    A leaked registration listing gives 192.7 g. The DJI Neo 2 weighs 151 g, so the difference is about 42 g, or 28%.

    Will the DJI Neo 3 be sold in the US?

    Probably not through DJI. DroneXL finds no FCC grant for the Neo 3. No new DJI drone has won US authorization since the FCC’s December 22, 2025 Covered List action. Models approved earlier stay legal to sell.

    Does the DJI Neo 3 shoot native vertical video?

    The leaked sheet says yes. It gives no resolution or frame rate for vertical clips.
